appliedUpdates.description: Updated .factory/library/architecture.md to correct the backend class hierarchy (TritonAttentionBackend instead of RocmAttentionBackend), fix the registration approach (TRITON_ATTN override instead of ROCM_ATTN/CUSTOM), update vLLM dual routing documentation, and add HIP graph compatibility requirements section.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Update the 'CORRECT approach' for backend registration to use TRITON_ATTN override instead of ROCM_ATTN. Current AGENTS.md says: 'register_backend(AttentionBackendEnum.ROCM_ATTN, ...)' but ROCM_ATTN is not the default backend selected on ROCm for standard attention -- TRITON_ATTN is. Using ROCM_ATTN will not intercept full-attention layer processing.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Feature create-tq-backend-and-register went through 3 iterations (CUSTOM → ROCM_ATTN → TRITON_ATTN) before finding the working approach. The fix is documented in commit d4fa1b7e7 and vllm_rocm.py docstring. Two separate commits (6c64563b7, d4fa1b7e7) show the worker had to discover this empirically despite AGENTS.md guidance.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add HIP graph compatibility requirements for any code running in graph-captured forward passes: (1) torch.randn() and similar RNG calls must use device='cpu', (2) tensors used in forward() must be pre-registered via register_buffer() not created dynamically, (3) TQ state initialization must happen in __init__. This knowledge is needed for hybrid-decode implementation as well.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Feature fix-tq-graph-mode-init was a dedicated fix feature created because capture-mode-correctness-validation failed graph mode across 5 worker sessions. The root cause was lazy initialization + dynamic tensor creation in forward(). This pattern will apply to hybrid-decode Triton kernel integration in the next milestone.

rejectedObservations.observation: Class-level _layer_counter in TurboQuantTritonImpl may not reset between model loads
rejectedObservations.reason: Non-blocking in current single-model deployment. Not worth a library update as this is an implementation detail of the TQ backend, not a vLLM or mission convention.

rejectedObservations.observation: VRAM test used 25 requests instead of the contract's 50
rejectedObservations.reason: The VRAM stability observed (0% change over 25 requests) provides strong enough evidence. The difference between 25 and 50 is not meaningful for detecting VRAM leaks.
Administrative data quality issue in features.json, not a code or knowledge gap. Not actionable via library or AGENTS.md update.
